caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 539 of 1991 with CR 105 (FM) of 1991.
lawyer:
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
M Nurullah with AQM Shafiullah, Advocates ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Aslam Hossain Chaklader ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Ali Nur and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the appellant Aslam Hossain Chaklader was granted lease for collection of tolls of Fatullah Hat and Bazar for 1398 BS by auction sale held on 11.4.91, being the highest bidder for Tk. 9,05,000.00 and the bid was accepted by the Upazila Parishad on 22.4.91. The appellant paid Tk. 2,40,000.00 on the date of the bid and he deposited balance money of Tk. 6,66,000.00 on 22.4.91 and he was put in possession of the Bazar on that day. The appellant was collecting tolls on and from 22.4.91. The plaintiff-respondents filed Title Suit No. 36 of 1991 on 27.4.91 against the appellant and Upazila Chairman and Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Narayanganj and another Ramjan Ali for a declaration that the order by the defendant No. 2 appointing defendant No. 1 as ejarader of the suit hat for 1398 BS on the basis of the auction sale of the Hat that took place on 11.4.91 in pursuance of notice dated 28.3.91 is illegal, without jurisdiction, etc. The plaintiff also filed a petition for temporary injunction under Order 39 rule 1 and section 151 CPC for restraining the defendant No. 1 from collecting tolls from the suit Hat pending disposal of the suit. The defendant- appellant appeared in Court and filed written objection against the prayer for temporary injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the parties allowed the petition for temporary injunction and restrained defendant No. 1 from collecting tolls from the suit Hat He has further ordered that the Fatullah Union Hat-Bazar Management Committee will collect the tolls of the suit Hat. 

 4. The plaintiff alleged that the notice inviting tender was illegal and it was not widely circulated, that the suit Hat cannot be leased out by auction sale for an amount not less than Tk. 20,00,000.00. He further alleged that he was prevented by armed Mastans from submitting his tender on the date fixed for the purpose. He made similar other allegations in the plaint. The defendant as usual denied the allegations made in the plaint The defence case was that there was no disturbance at the time of submitting the tender, the bid was held peacefully and normally and he being the highest bidder amongst the 11 tenderers his bid was accepted and the suit Hat was leased out to him for the year 1398 BS and he will sustain a great loss and injury if he is now restrained from collecting tolls after purchase of the ejara by his good money. It is further alleged that the suit is not maintainable as no notice was served under section 80 of the Local Government (Upazila Parishad and Upazila Administration Re-organization) Ordinance 1982. 

 5. It is admitted that the appellant being the highest bidder was granted the lease for collection of tolls from the suit Hat for the year 1398 BS. The plaintiff admittedly could not participate in the bid as they were allegedly obstructed by the armed miscreants for submitting the tender to the authority. The plaintiffs-respondents have therefore no prima facie claim or authority to collect tolls from the suit Hat for the year 1398 BS. If they sustain any injury or loss due to the alleged illegality or irregularities in holding the auction, they may realise compensation for the same, in case the suit is decreed. As the defendant-appellant is the admitted purchaser of the Hat in auction for collecting tolls for the year 1398 BS, he will certainly sustain injury and loss if he is restrained from collecting the tolls after payment of as much as Tk. 9,05,000.00 as the sale money. It is thus clear that the balance of convenience is in favour of the defendant-appellant while the plaintiff’s respondents could not make out any prima facie case for injunction. We are, therefore, of opinion that the learned Subordinate Judge was not justified in allowing the prayer for temporary injunction.
